hero.headline: Vero Beach shooting victim identified as Dawn Kriskewic, suspect Matthew Waggle still at large
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic.
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. Kriskewic was found with an apparent gunshot wound in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street Sunday morning. Despite life-saving measures by deputies, she was pronounced dead at a trauma center.

Detectives are treating the case as a domestic violence homicide and continue searching for 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle of Sebastian, who has been identified as a person of interest. Investigators believe Waggle and Kriskewic were in an on-and-off relationship. Sheriff Eric Flowers said a nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle, who should be considered armed and dangerous and may have fled the area.

The sheriff's office said there was a delay in releasing the victim's name because several out-of-state next of kin needed to be located and notified. Close friends remembered Kriskewic as someone who was beautiful inside and out, a mother, hairdresser and author who was loved by many.

Flowers warned residents not to approach Waggle. Anyone with information is asked to contact Det. Kachele at 772-978-6240 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers. Waggle is described as having brown hair and blue eyes, about 6 feet 1 inch tall and weighing about 200 pounds.

cards.headline: Left lane of I-95 southbound blocked near Stuart due to roadway debris
cards.teaser: The left lane of I-95 southbound is blocked in Martin County Tuesday morning due to roadway debris, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The blockage is on I-95 southbound near
cards.body:
The left lane of I-95 southbound is blocked in Martin County Tuesday morning due to roadway debris, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The blockage is on I-95 southbound near mile marker 101, before the SR-76/Kanner Highway exit in Stuart.

The highway was shut down for at least an hour before partially reopening, according to FL511. The Florida Highway Patrol says the left lane remains blocked while crews work to clear the roadway.

The incident is affecting southbound traffic on I-95 in Martin County. Drivers should expect delays in the area near the Kanner Highway exit.

Crews are working to clear the debris and fully reopen the southbound lanes. The Florida Highway Patrol is monitoring the situation as cleanup continues.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie voters head to polls Tuesday for mayoral election
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin faces challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in the city's mayoral race.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie voters shared their priorities for the city's next mayor as they cast ballots Tuesday. One voter said safety is most important to them, while another voiced concerns about development, saying it was so beautiful and a lot of it has gone to development after living in the city for 20 years.

Other voters focused on the type of leadership they want to see at city hall. One voter said they would like the mayor to be somebody that has lived here, worked here, knows what it's like to be a working person, has kids, wants to keep them here, raise them here so they have a good future. A majority of voters expressed a desire for a mayor who is honest and committed to addressing issues that matter to residents.

The race follows a campaign sign controversy that resulted in three Port St. Lucie police officers being placed on leave. Police say the investigation involves two incidents earlier this month. Surveillance video shows a woman removing one of Mayor Shannon Martin's campaign signs, with her opponent Steven Giordano seen at the scene. In another incident, Giordano reported witnessing someone vandalizing his campaign sign. The officers placed on leave are Lt. Jason Vega, Detective Joseph Alves, and Lt. Aaron Martin, who is the mayor's husband. Polling places in Port St. Lucie are open until 7 p.m.

cards.headline: Indian River County Sheriff's Office uses Flock cameras in search for Vero Beach homicide suspect
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office is using a network of automated license plate cameras and its Real Time Crime Center to search for Matthew Waggle.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed Tuesday it has been using its Real Time Crime Center and a network of Flock license plate cameras as investigators search for 33-year-old Matthew Waggle and work to piece together what happened in the Sunday morning homicide of 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. Waggle has been identified as a person of interest in the shooting death of Kriskewic, who was found in the 500 block of First Street, just outside Vero Beach, Sunday morning.

A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle. Investigators say he should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached. The Sheriff's Office said investigators believe Kriskewic had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the shooting as a domestic violence homicide.

The Sheriff's Office said there are no further updates ready for release at this time. The investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Miami woman accused of posing as bank representative in Martin County credit card scam
cards.teaser: A Florida woman took a scam beyond phone lines, showing up at a Martin County resident's door pretending to represent a bank and demanding a credit card on Monday.
cards.body:
Monique Love Turnbull, of Miami, was seen at a victim's doorstep claiming the victim's bank account had been compromised, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Turnbull asked for the victim's credit card and said she would dispose of it. As law enforcement investigated, deputies were alerted to another call identifying Turnbull in a separate case.

Body camera video shows deputies pulling Turnbull over and asking her to step out of the car. The arresting deputy then tells Turnbull she is under arrest for fraud before placing her in handcuffs.

The sheriff's office is warning residents never to allow someone into their home if the person was not scheduled to visit. Residents should also never hand over credit cards, cash, gold or other valuables to someone who shows up unexpectedly. MCSO says anyone who comes to a resident's home claiming to represent a bank or financial institution and asking for valuables should be treated with suspicion. Residents are urged to call 911.

cards.headline: Shannon Ramsey-Chessman sworn in as interim Palm Beach County clerk after Michael Caruso arrest
cards.teaser: Shannon Ramsey-Chessman was sworn in Tuesday as Clerk Ad Interim after Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso was arrested on five felony child sex abuse charges and immediately suspended from office by Gov. Ron DeSantis.
cards.body:
Chief Judge Glenn Kelley of the 15th Judicial Circuit issued an administrative order Tuesday naming Ramsey-Chessman to the role, effective immediately. The appointment follows Caruso's arrest on charges including kidnapping, lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, luring or enticing a child, and child abuse causing mental injury, according to an arrest warrant and affidavit filed in Orange County Circuit Court.

Ramsey-Chessman has served as Chief Deputy Clerk, Chief of Staff and Chief Information Officer for the Palm Beach County Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller since January 2021, according to court records. Her 29 years of public sector experience includes working with Palm Beach County's Office of Financial Management and Budget, the 15th Judicial Circuit, and the Martin County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller.

Caruso, 67, faces serious charges stemming from allegations involving a child victim over nearly a year-long period. Caruso was appointed to the Palm Beach County Clerk position in August 2025 by DeSantis, following seven years of service in the Florida House of Representatives. He is running for election in November to retain his position, but his name is not on Tuesday's primary ballot since he is running uncontested.

cards.headline: Martin County deputies rescue man attempting suicide in ocean
cards.teaser:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County
cards.body:
Two divisions of the Martin County Sheriff's Office worked together Sunday to save a man suffering from a mental health crisis. The sheriff's office released a video from Sunday, August 16, showing Marine Deputies and the Aviation Unit working with a Martin County Lifeguard to rescue a man who was distraught and wanting to harm himself.

The man stated he was going to swim out into the ocean in hopes of not returning, according to the sheriff's office. When personnel located the man, they observed he was in emotional distress. Deputies entered the water and pulled the man out.

The sheriff's office said the man is getting the help he needs. The Suicide Crisis Lifeline is available by calling or texting 988, or through online chat. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or texting a ZIP code to 898211.

hero.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
hero.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
hero.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

The incident is affecting southbound traffic on I-95 in Martin County. Drivers should expect delays in the area near the Kanner Highway exit.

Crews are working to clear the debris and fully reopen the southbound lanes. The Florida Highway Patrol is monitoring the situation as cleanup continues.

cards.headline: Martin County deputies rescue man attempting suicide in ocean
cards.teaser:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County
cards.body:
Two divisions of the Martin County Sheriff's Office worked together Sunday to save a man suffering from a mental health crisis. The sheriff's office released a video from Sunday, August 16, showing Marine Deputies and the Aviation Unit working with a Martin County Lifeguard to rescue a man who was distraught and wanting to harm himself.

The man stated he was going to swim out into the ocean in hopes of not returning, according to the sheriff's office. When personnel located the man, they observed he was in emotional distress. Deputies entered the water and pulled the man out.

The sheriff's office said the man is getting the help he needs. The Suicide Crisis Lifeline is available by calling or texting 988, or through online chat. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or texting a ZIP code to 898211.

cards.headline: Shannon Ramsey-Chessman sworn in as interim Palm Beach County clerk after Michael Caruso arrest
cards.teaser: Shannon Ramsey-Chessman was sworn in Tuesday as Clerk Ad Interim after Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso was arrested on five felony child sex abuse charges and immediately suspended from office by Gov. Ron DeSantis.
cards.body:
Chief Judge Glenn Kelley of the 15th Judicial Circuit issued an administrative order Tuesday naming Ramsey-Chessman to the role, effective immediately. The appointment follows Caruso's arrest on charges including kidnapping, lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, luring or enticing a child, and child abuse causing mental injury, according to an arrest warrant and affidavit filed in Orange County Circuit Court.

 Ramsey-Chessman has served as Chief Deputy Clerk, Chief of Staff and Chief Information Officer for the Palm Beach County Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller since January 2021, according to court records. Her 29 years of public sector experience includes working with Palm Beach County's Office of Financial Management and Budget, the 15th Judicial Circuit, and the Martin County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller.

 Caruso, 67, faces serious charges stemming from allegations involving a child victim over nearly a year-long period. Caruso was appointed to the Palm Beach County Clerk position in August 2025 by DeSantis, following seven years of service in the Florida House of Representatives. He is running for election in November to retain his position, but his name is not on Tuesday's primary ballot since he is running uncontested.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie voters head to polls Tuesday for mayoral election
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin faces challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in the city's mayoral race.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie voters shared their priorities for the city's next mayor as they cast ballots Tuesday. One voter said safety is most important to them, while another voiced concerns about development, saying it was so beautiful and a lot of it has gone to development after living in the city for 20 years.

Other voters focused on the type of leadership they want to see at city hall. One voter said they would like the mayor to be somebody that has lived here, worked here, knows what it's like to be a working person, has kids, wants to keep them here, raise them here so they have a good future. A majority of voters expressed a desire for a mayor who is honest and committed to addressing issues that matter to residents.

The race follows a campaign sign controversy that resulted in three Port St. Lucie police officers being placed on leave. Police say the investigation involves two incidents earlier this month. Surveillance video shows a woman removing one of Mayor Shannon Martin's campaign signs, with her opponent Steven Giordano seen at the scene. In another incident, Giordano reported witnessing someone vandalizing his campaign sign. The officers placed on leave are Lt. Jason Vega, Detective Joseph Alves, and Lt. Aaron Martin, who is the mayor's husband. Polling places in Port St. Lucie are open until 7 p.m.

hero.headline: Indian River County Sheriff's Office uses Flock cameras in search for Vero Beach homicide suspect
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office is using a network of automated license plate cameras and its Real Time Crime Center to search for Matthew Waggle.
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed Tuesday it has been using its Real Time Crime Center and a network of Flock license plate cameras as investigators search for 33-year-old Matthew Waggle and work to piece together what happened in the Sunday morning homicide of 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. Waggle has been identified as a person of interest in the shooting death of Kriskewic, who was found in the 500 block of First Street, just outside Vero Beach, Sunday morning.

A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle. Investigators say he should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached. The Sheriff's Office said investigators believe Kriskewic had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the shooting as a domestic violence homicide.

The Sheriff's Office said there are no further updates ready for release at this time. The investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Vero Beach shooting victim identified as Dawn Kriskewic, suspect Matthew Waggle still at large
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office has identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. Kriskewic was found with an apparent gunshot wound in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street Sunday morning. Despite life-saving measures by deputies, she was pronounced dead at a trauma center.

The sheriff's office said there was a delay in releasing the victim's name because several out-of-state next of kin needed to be located and notified. Detectives are treating the case as a domestic violence homicide and continue searching for 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle of Sebastian, who has been identified as a person of interest. Investigators believe Waggle and Kriskewic were in an on-and-off relationship.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said a nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle, who should be considered armed and dangerous and may have fled the area. Flowers warned residents not to approach Waggle if they encounter him, saying it is possible he could harm other people or himself.

Close friends remembered Kriskewic as someone who was beautiful inside and out, a mother, hairdresser and author who was loved by many. The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact Det. Kachele at 772-978-6240 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.
